question: What percentage of households were classified as the poorest of the poor, as per SECC-2011?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**0.89%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011**, a certain percentage of households were classified as the **poorest of the poor**.
 
• The SECC 2011 was a comprehensive survey conducted to identify households living below the poverty line and collect data about their socio-economic conditions.
 
• The classification as "poorest of the poor" is based on multiple indicators such as **income levels, assets, housing conditions, and access to basic amenities.**
 
• The correct percentage in this context is **0.0089**, which denotes the proportion of households identified under this category.
 
• This data is crucial for the formulation of targeted policies and programs by the government to address extreme poverty and improve the living conditions of affected households.
 
• SECC 2011 not only aids in identifying beneficiaries for various welfare schemes but also provides a detailed understanding of **socio-economic disparities** across different regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011**__

 __
 
• **SECC 2011** was conducted jointly by the Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation, and the Registrar General of India.
 
• The SECC collected data on various aspects such as **education, employment, caste, housing, and income levels**.
 
• The SECC was instrumental in identifying beneficiaries for government schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana** and **National Food Security Act.**
 
 
 
• **Indicators Used for Classification**__
 
 
• The classification of households under categories like "poorest of the poor" was based on indicators such as **household income, access to drinking water, sanitation facilities, and employment type.**
 
• These indicators help in determining the extent of deprivation and socio-economic challenges faced by households.
